ResearchProjectDef.label: Plumbing valve
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a valve that opens or closes connections between pipes.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Water well
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a water well that provides groundwater for manual collection. Water can be hauled to tubs for washing or drinking.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Water tub
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a tub that holds water for personal hygiene. Must be regularly refilled with fresh water, also fills with rain water. Can also be used for drinking if thirst is enabled.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Stall door
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a thin door that blocks line of sight to people using bathroom fixtures. Does not create new rooms or prevent heat loss.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Bath Mat
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a small mat used next to a bathtub to absorb water.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Water Trough
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a trough that supplies water for animals. A service box with a ballcock valve automatically refills it when the water level is low, and rain also replenishes it.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Water Bowl
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a bowl that holds drinking water for animals.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Burn pit
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a burn pit that eliminates fecal sludge by burning it as fuel. Can also be used for disposing of corpses or other detritus. Colonists may become sick if they spend too long near burning waste.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Groundwater intake
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a groundwater intake that supplies groundwater to connected pumps. It cannot be operated manually. The presence of sewage or other pollution will reduce water quality and can cause contamination.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Water butt
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a water butt that stores water for use by plumbed fixtures. Slowly fills when raining. The water must be drained if it becomes contaminated. Capacity: 100.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Water tower
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a water tower that stores water for use by plumbed fixtures. The water must be drained if it becomes contaminated. Capacity: 8000.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Wind pump
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a wind pump that pumps water from wells to water towers. Pumping capacity: 3000 L/day.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Huge water tower
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a huge water tower that stores water for use by plumbed fixtures. The water must be drained if it becomes contaminated. Capacity: 50,000.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Shower
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a shower that uses water supplied by water towers. Can be heated via plumbed hot water tanks. Does not require a sewage outlet.\n65L per wash

ResearchProjectDef.label: Shower stall
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a shower stall that uses water supplied by water towers. Can be heated via plumbed hot water tanks. Does not require a sewage outlet.\n65L per wash

ResearchProjectDef.label: Drinking fountain
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a water fountain used for drinking and washing.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Kitchen sink
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a kitchen sink that increases room cleanliness.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Hot water tank
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a hot water tank that stores hot running water for showers and baths. Connect to any boiler to heat.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Surface water intake
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a pipe laid into open fresh water, facing the water, which can be pumped by water pumps like a well. Rivers provide the most water, then lakes; marsh water provides the least and is stagnant, contaminating the water it is pumped into. Sea water can't be used.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Latrine
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a pit latrine that collects faeces in a hole in the ground. Must be emptied manually, or can be plumbed.\n14L per use

ResearchProjectDef.label: Litter box
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build an indoor faeces and urine collection box for small animals.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Sewage outlet
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a sewage outlet that can be placed anywhere. Sewage will pool and spread on land or disperse in water. Sewage cleans up over time; the presence of trees, water, or rain will speed this up.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Basin
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a bathroom basin that lets colonists wash their hands after using the toilet.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Bathtub
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a bathtub that provides a comfortable, leisurely wash. Can be heated by placing an adjacent campfire or log boiler, or via plumbed hot water tanks. Does not require a sewage outlet.\n190L per wash

ResearchProjectDef.label: Chemfuel boiler
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build a chemfuel boiler that produces 2000 heating units for radiators and hot water tanks. Requires chemfuel for fuel. Can be controlled by thermostats.

ResearchProjectDef.label: Electric boiler
ResearchProjectDef.description: Build an electric boiler that produces a variable amount of heating units for radiators and hot water tanks. Manually controlled power setting. Can be controlled by thermostats.
